packages.name: win32
packages.description: Call common Windows APIs directly from Dart using FFI.
packages.oneLiner: Call common Windows APIs and COM objects directly from Dart using FFI.

explainer.whatItDoes: Exposes a curated surface of Win32 and COM APIs via Dart FFI. Enables Windows-specific capabilities that are not accessible through standard dart:io or Flutter plugins.
useWhen: Building Flutter desktop apps for Windows that require low-level system or hardware access.
Writing cross-platform packages with a Windows-specific native backend.
Developing command-line tools or background services on Windows needing native file, process, or security APIs.
avoidWhen: Targeting non-Windows platforms like Android, iOS, or macOS.
Building standard multiplatform apps where regular Flutter plugins or dart:io provide sufficient functionality.
strengths: Provides direct, low-level access to Win32 and COM APIs in Dart.
Eliminates the need for MSVC to build native wrappers in recent versions.
Supports robust error handling and modern FFI usage.
weaknesses: Restricted entirely to the Windows platform.
Requires manual resource management and dealing with raw platform pointers.
explainer.setupNotes: Works out of the box on Windows targets; no local MSVC compiler is strictly required for default prebuilt binaries.
